1800.author: Jianyu010
1800.body:
Refs #1786 #1749

Depended on openJiuwen-ai/DigitalMate#1797 (#1783 base), now merged; origin/main is merged in.

## What

Bee-only write/exec lane, plugged in by the §2.1 recipe (catalog rows, `handlers/write_exec.py`, one `HANDLER_MODULES` line, tests). No base API change.

- `write_file` (`write`), `edit_file` (`search_replace`): agent-core `WriteFileTool` / `EditFileTool` via `invoke_agentcore`. Their only write path is the lane's `FS_METHODS["write_file"]`: per-component `O_NOFOLLOW` opens from the task root, private temp file + `fsync`, recheck the target is still the same plain single-link file (and, for edits, the same content sha256), then atomic `rename`.
- `bash` (`mcp_exec_command`): agent-core `BashTool` on a lane `WorkspaceShell`. cwd = the link-free root descriptor (`fchdir`). Env = allowlist minus credential-like names (`[tools.env]` on the `bash` row). HOME/TMPDIR = task root. Timeout, command and output caps come from `[tools.limits]`. The process group is killed on timeout or Stop. No background runs, no `workdir`. Output stays under the cap, so it never spills to the shared `/tmp/openjiuwen_bash_outputs`.
- `powershell`: platform-gated. The row is enabled with a handler, but `bee = false`, so it is not in the Bee set or the rail. The handler says "platform not applicable" on Linux.
- `create_terminal`: still forbidden. Beebou gets none of these tools.
- All four run as gate bound effects: the plan is persisted first, the `operation_id` receipt replays, and a started-but-unfinished call is UNKNOWN and never re-run.

The deny patterns live in `[tools.env]`, not `[tools.limits]`, because the base parser accepts only positive integers in limits.

Two base tests asserted that write/exec rows were still reserved. They now use row-agnostic assertions (reserved rows never callable; read set has no journaled tools). No base code changed.

## Matrix rows

| Tool (alias) | Bee / Beebou | Host mapping | Status here | Evidence | Blocker |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `write_file` (`write`) | on / off | bound effect → WriteFileTool → O_NOFOLLOW atomic write | unit verified; device pending #1790 | write then read in same task visible, other task not; other task / room / Bee home / `..` / symlink / swapped dir / swapped file all refused without content or Host path; replay once; UNKNOWN not re-run; Stop at commit point leaves the old file and no temp | none |
| `edit_file` (`search_replace`) | on / off | same, EditFileTool + sha256 recheck | same | edit visible to later read; same refusals | none |
| `bash` (`mcp_exec_command`) | on / off | bound effect → BashTool → WorkspaceShell | **open, isolation unproven (shared container, no OS-level path/network isolation); same uid can read/forge Host receipts and other tasks' dirs (B2)**; tracked in #1840 (deferred) | runs in task root; credential env (`*_API_KEY`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `AWS_SECRET_*`) invisible; timeout kills the group; output capped, no spill; Stop mid-call (gate `release_lane`) kills the real shell group within 3 s and the plan stays PLANNED/UNKNOWN, never EXECUTED (B10); replay does not repeat | **yes: B1, B2, B15 → #1840 (deferred; owner accepted shipping with them)** |
| `powershell` | platform-gated (n/a on Linux) / off | refusal only | refused | `test_powershell_is_platform_gated`, exposure test | none |

## Residual risk / blocker B1

The shell shares the container with the Host and WorkSwarm. It can reach any path the process can, including:

- other task dirs and the receipts dir;
- the shared WorkSwarm home `<workspace>/bee-workswarm/` (WorkSwarm memory, cron and skill files for all of this user's Bees);
- room data, config, and the network.

The cwd, HOME, env allowlist, foreground-only rule and process-group kill shrink accidental reach. None of them is isolation. Command-text path filtering is deliberately not added: it is bypassable and would overclaim. A real fix needs OS-level isolation: a per-task sandbox `SysOperation` backend, a separate uid, or mount/network namespaces. Details: `docs/implementations/contracts/hive-tool-access-1786.md` §3.

## Owner decision on B1 / B2

Jianyu010 decided on 2026-11-17 to ship `bash` with the B1/B2 residuals as documented. Bash isolation is a general sandbox concern, not a Hive-specific one, and is tracked in #1840 (deferred). The matrix row stays "open, isolation unproven".

The #1790 coordinator accepted B1 and the receipts exposure (B2) as residuals on the same basis (QA round 2). The lane doc §3 records the decision with the #1840 link.

**B15 (QA round 3):** `setsid sleep 300 & echo started` returns at once, but the detached process (parent pid 1, its own session, cwd in the task) outlives the call, because the group kill cannot reach it. This is the `setsid` gap already named in contract §3, mitigation 3. It is a process-isolation escape, so it is a residual under B1. The #1790 coordinator ruled it non-blocking for this PR. The repro is recorded on #1840 (deferred).

## Stop / revocation during a call (#1790 B10)

QA round 2 pressed Stop 23 s into `sleep 60`: the Run ended `stopped`, but the shell ran to the 45 s timeout and `host-gate` then settled the plan EXECUTED. Cause: the gate's Stop / revocation only releases the lane (`release_lane`), which never reaches a call already executing.

- `AgentCoreEffectProvider.bound_effect` now re-checks `lane_identity` every `lane_poll_ms` (catalog, 200 ms on the write/edit/bash rows) while the call runs. If the lane was released or rebound to another Task or Run, it cancels the call (bash: kill and reap the process group), keeps the receipt `started`, and raises UNKNOWN. The gate then returns `unknown`, the plan stays PLANNED, reconciliation keeps it UNKNOWN, and it is never re-run.
- A second race: a cancel landing while asyncio was still connecting the new shell's pipes made asyncio kill only the shell, leaving its children. `WorkspaceShell` now lets the spawn complete, then kills and reaps the whole group before the cancellation propagates.
- **Base touch:** the watch is a behavior fix in the base `temp/hive-tools/src/dm_hive_tools/providers.py` (`apply_bound` plus `_while_bound`). No API change. Rows without `lane_poll_ms` (e.g. `deliver_file`) behave as before.
- Tests (real subprocesses): hive-tools `test_stop_releasing_the_lane_kills_a_running_bash_at_once`, `test_a_lane_rebound_to_another_run_also_stops_the_call`, `test_a_cancel_while_the_shell_is_spawning_kills_its_whole_group` (fails without the spawn fix). Bridge `test_hive_bee_bash_stop.py` uses the real gate (admit → execute → `release_lane`): decision `unknown`, plan PLANNED, never EXECUTED, shell group gone.

## Blocker B2: Host receipts and other task dirs are reachable from bash

Operation receipts live in `<workspace>/hive-tasks-host/receipts/`, beside the task directories. `bash` runs as the Host uid, so `cd ../..` or any absolute path reaches them.

- **Read:** a receipt stores the full result of each write/exec call, so a Bee can read other tasks' command output. It can also read and write other tasks' work files.
- **Forge or tamper:**
  - A planted `started` receipt pins that `operation_id` to UNKNOWN (DoS).
  - A planted `done` receipt for an operation ID it can predict is replayed as that operation's result.
  - A deleted receipt makes a finished operation look never-started.

This lane has no cheap fix. Under the same uid, moving receipts outside the cwd tree does not stop absolute paths, and command-text filtering is bypassable. Mitigations outside this lane, none claimed here:

1. **Base (#1797):** HMAC-sign receipts with a Host-only key (never in the bash env). Treat a bad MAC as UNKNOWN. This stops forged replay, not reads or deletion.
2. **Base:** keep receipts in the Store, in the journal transaction, not on the workspace disk.
3. **Deploy:** run bash as a dedicated low-privilege uid, with per-task directory permissions and receipts readable only by the Host. Whether the current deploy can switch uid is unverified.

B2 stays a blocker until one of these lands and is verified. Doc §3 has the details.

## Phase B (#1790)

No new env vars. Once #1783's Bee tool config is on, `write_file` / `edit_file` / `bash` appear in the Bee set and the rail, and `powershell` does not. Tunables are in `tools.toml` (see doc §4).

## Evidence

- hk-longjianyu at `2aeaac3c` (main `c58b8609` merged): hive-tools 147/147 (3 repeated runs); Bridge B10 test 5/5 repeated runs; Hive Bridge subset 72/72; architecture check clean; no leftover processes after the runs.
- Local focused: `test_hive_tools_write_exec` 18/18; base catalog/workspace/providers 25/25.
- hk-longjianyu (py3.13, wheel venv with the PR's `temp/*/src` on the path) at `7d15a232` (main `dea14df1` merged): hive-tools 142/142; Hive Bridge tool/Beebou/deliver/product-search/memory/attachment tests 62/62; architecture check clean.
- Base-test touch-ups after the merge: write/exec tests now pass the Host binding (`attach_lanes`), with a new test that an unbound or other-Task lane never runs. In the Bridge `test_hive_bee_tools`, the exposure set now includes the write/exec names, the expected set is compared only with the offered names, and `powershell` is in the hidden list. After #1784 merged: its read tests now check the read set exactly and check write/exec as Bee-only (no longer "hidden"). The Bridge Beebou catalog assertion now expects the five read tools; it was stale on main since #1784.

1802.body:
Refs #1788 #1749

**Depends on #1797** (the #1783 base: `HostBinding`, `CallContext.service`). It is built on #1797 at `0069c8bd`. It merges only after #1797 is on main.

## What
This PR adds Host-side read tools `native_search_memory`, `native_read_memory` and `native_search_conversations` for **Bees** (gate readers) and **Beebou** (Plugin Gateway). Beebou had no memory read tool before this.

| Piece | File |
| --- | --- |
| Lane handlers (3 tools, argument policy, fence, tagging) | `temp/hive-tools/src/dm_hive_tools/handlers/memory.py` |
| Catalog rows enabled + limits; `HANDLER_MODULES` line | `config/tools.toml`, `handlers/__init__.py` |
| **Temporary adapter**: product memory/history read port | `agent_bridge/src/server_engine/hive_memory_reads.py` (ownership: `hive-tools-memory-reads`) |
| **Temporary adapter**: Hive Global Memory read port | `temp/hive-tools/src/dm_hive_tools/handlers/memory_ports.py` |
| Injection | `server.py` builds `hive_memory_services(engine, scope.workspace_id)` and passes it to `register_hive_tools(workspace, services)` and, through a new `compose_bee_runtime(tool_services=...)` pass-through, to `bee_host_tools(adapter, services)` |

## Rules enforced
- **Product read APIs only. No new store, no new writer, no cache.** The port calls `EngineMemory.search_async`, `get_record_async` and `revalidate_records` with the person's Home access. History uses `engine_recall.related_turns`, with the per-turn checks of the `conversation.search` action. Every text passes through `for_agents`. It does **not** call the engine actions `memory.search` / `memory.read` / `conversation.search`, because those write: they set `_pin_memory_recall` and `task.recalled`.
- **Scope from the Host binding only.** The engine serves one principal in one workspace. A call reads only when `owner_id == engine.principal_id` and `room_id == workspace name`, matching how Hive builds `AuthenticatedScope`. Memories kept for one conversation are never shown. History searches only rooms the person alone shares with agents. Items that are outside the binding are dropped by the handler.
- **Global Memory only when explicitly authorized.** `include_global` must be set, the `global_memory` service must be injected, and `authorized(binding)` must return true. **No Host grant for Global Memory reads exists yet, so it is not injected and is never read.** The port is ready for that grant. It follows the approach of draft #1750 by huben0423-hw: it reads the surface twice and refuses if `surface_rev` moved.
- **Source and scope on every result.** The handler sets the tag (`product_memory` / `conversation_history` / `hive_global_memory`, plus `scope.reach` and `scope.room_id`); the port does not.
- **Nothing on refusal.** A refusal, a closed fence, a port error and an empty result all return the same text: `No memory is available for this request.`
- **Revoke / Stop fence.** The `live(binding)` check runs before the read and again before disclosure. Each call reads again, so a forget or a revoke reaches the next call.
- Old WorkSwarm memory tools stay forbidden in the catalog.

## Evidence (matrix rows)
| Tool | Bee | Beebou | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| native_search_memory | on | on | `test_hive_tools_memory` (fake port, real catalog / CallContext / HostBinding); `test_hive_memory_reads` (real EngineService) |
| native_read_memory | on | on | same |
| native_search_conversations | on | on | same |
| read changes nothing | — | — | `test_a_read_changes_no_byte_of_the_stores`: sha256 of every store file and WAL, and the task rows, are unchanged after Bee and Beebou reads |

hk-longjianyu, wheel install at `3467e47cd` (Python 3.13):
- `temp/hive-tools` unittest discover: **48 tests OK**
- Bridge pytest `test_hive_memory_reads`, `test_hive_bee_tools`, `test_hive_beebou_agentcore`, `test_runtime_wheels`, `test_engine_memory_redaction`: **35 passed**
- `tools/architecture/check.py`: **clean** (299 of 541 files)

The shared set tests (`test_hive_tools_providers`, `test_hive_bee_tools` exposure, `test_hive_beebou_agentcore` registry) now include the three memory names. Other lanes edit the same lines, so the second lane to merge resolves the set.

## Pod env for #1790
No extra env. The memory tools are on whenever Hive tools are wired (`host_tools`), with the default catalog.

## Known limits
- This is a temporary adapter until Memory publishes an authorized-read interface (#1647 / #999).
- Text the model has already seen is not taken back after a later revoke; that belongs to Session Store context invalidation (#1491).
- Edits to shared files beyond the recipe: a `tool_services` pass-through in `compose_bee_runtime`, the only caller of `bee_host_tools`; the adapter entry plus a `legacy-mobile-gateway` caller in `temp/hive-tools/ownership.json`; and the expected tool sets in the three shared tests.
- History retention fails closed. Turns that draw on a non-retained or Slack source are not shown, which is stricter than the product's `_retention_allowed`, a private method the gate forbids calling here.

Refs #1787 #1749

**Depends on #1797 (#1783 base).** This branch sits on the #1783 base; it is rebased onto main and merged only after #1797 lands.

## What changes

| Tool | Bee | Beebou |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ask_user` | existing Host question channel and wait point (`host_ask`, never the effect gate) | — |
| `todo_create` / `todo_get` / `todo_list` / `todo_modify` | on by default through the catalog; plan keyed by (runtime Session, Task) | — |
| `skill_tool` | bundled skills (runtime reader) | new `SkillToolProvider` over the DM-owned `<workspace>/beebou-skills`, via Plugin Gateway (`tool/agentcore-skills/1`) |
| `search_skill` / `install_skill` / `uninstall_skill` | **disabled — blocker** | not offered |
| `todo_insert` / `todo_complete` / `todo_remove` | forbidden (also as an alias) | — |

- **Catalog → Registry (no stranded Bees).** With the planner and skill rows on, the WorkSwarm Bee factory is also registered as `tools_harness_version = "2"` (`bee_runtime.toml`). New Bee Sessions bind v2. A Session already bound to v1 keeps its exact profile: `ready_for` / `routing_status` accept it, and the rail keeps planner and skills off for it.
- **Task scoping.** The gate answers a new `lane` rail request with the bound Task's digest and whether the lane's exact profile has the runtime tools. The rail keys `todo.json` by (runtime Session, Task): a Task switch parks the previous plan under `hive-plans/<digest>.json` and restores its own. Another Bee's Session, an earlier profile, Stop or revocation (`current()` false or lane released) get nothing, and exposure follows the same answer per model call.
- **Beebou skills.** `dm_hive_tools.skills` (additive; `ToolHandler` / `CallContext` / `AgentCoreToolProvider` unchanged) runs agent-core `SkillTool` on a `WorkspaceOperation` bound to the skills root (`O_NOFOLLOW` resolver). Settings in `config/skills.toml`.

## Blocker (recorded)
`install_skill` / `uninstall_skill` / `search_skill` stay disabled. All Bees of a user share one WorkSwarm process and home (`<workspace>/bee-workswarm`); `SkillManager` and the SkillTool listing are process-global and the runtime does not know which Bee a Session serves, so a Bee-private install target is not clean. `search_skill` alone would call online skill markets with nothing to install.

## Evidence matrix

1808.body:
## Summary
- based on latest `main`
- remove the global Bee processing/stop strip from the Home composer
- expose `停止此任务` only after selecting a Bee and expanding its 会话记录 in Beebou 实时活动
- bind the action to the selected Bee's current `run.taskRef` and preserve stop receipt/retry handling

## Related issues
Closes #1765
Related to #1766 and #1767. The full backend streaming design remains separate; this PR only changes client placement and task-scoped stop behavior.

## Cloud scope
No server image, template, Binding, or cloud restart is required. The change is client-only and consumes the existing `busy_controls.stop` declaration plus `hive.bee.stop` contract.

1809.author: Jianyu010
1809.body:
Refs #1644

This is the real-model acceptance #1644 asks for: with several candidate Home conversations, Beebou should dispatch directly when the target is clear and ask when it is not. It reports the wrong-target rate and the ask rate.

## Changes

- **New case category `choice-card`** (`tests/eval/hive-live/cases/12-choice-card.json`). Three cases: CHOICE-01 and CHOICE-03 in Chinese, CHOICE-02 in English. In each case three Bees first finish three distinct tasks (a shopping list, a cleaning rota or packing plan, a trip, offsite or meeting). Then come 4 follow-ups:
  - 2 **clear** ones, e.g. "购物清单再加两样", "Add a vegetarian lunch option to the offsite agenda". Expected: `new:reuse`/`steer` to the right Bee, with `route.to` / `not_to`.
  - 2 **ambiguous** ones, e.g. "改成周四", "把其中一个改到周一", "Move it to Thursday.", "那个再加一点。" Expected: a `choice` card and zero dispatches.
- **Grader**
  - New decision atom `choice`: an `ask_choice` with an `accepted` receipt and no accepted dispatch (`[tools].choice`, `[receipts].choice_ok`). `ask_choice` is in `[tools].read_only`, because it is a BOT_READ under contract C1.
  - New expectation key `choice: {from, min}`, checked by `live_choice`. The options' `task_ref`s must cover at least `min` of the candidate Bees, otherwise FAIL. A card that reaches the count only through options without `task_ref` is UNREASONABLE. An option on a Bee outside `from` is UNREASONABLE.
  - Self-tests for the signature, the card check and the validator. Case-count caps raised from 50 to 60, and the category count from 11 to 12.
- **Docs:** `docs/scenarios/hive-behaviour-qa.md` has the new signature and check rows, a results section and the regenerated catalogue.

## Results

Run `1644-choice-4371a5ec`:
- Server `4371a5ec` (main), suite `9e500b19`.
- `local_cli` with the launcher, product model `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017` through the hp-laptop csi relay. The probe passed (3/3 calls returned 200, p50 10.7 s).
- 3 cases × 3 repeats = 36 follow-up turns, 373 model calls, about 3.8M tokens.

Artifacts (outside the repo): `DigitalMate-tools/hive-live-artifacts/1644-choice-4371a5ec/`, including `report.md`, `grades.json`, `rates.txt` and `choice-rates-1644.mjs`.

| Metric | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Ask rate on ambiguous turns (`ask_choice` card) | **15/18 = 83%**. No text-only asks. 15/17 = 88% without the one turn whose setup was not met |
| Guessed on ambiguous turns (any dispatch attempt) | **3/18 = 17%**: 2 accepted, 1 refused `not_granted` |
| Cards with the right candidates (≥ 2, with `task_ref`) | 13/15. The other 2 had the right labels but no `task_ref` at all |
| Clear turns dispatched directly to the right Bee | **18/18 = 100%**, all `new` + `follows` to that Bee's original task |
| Wrong-target rate on clear turns | **0/18 = 0%** |
| Over-ask rate on clear turns | **0/18 = 0%** |

Per case (ambiguous asked / clear correct):
- CHOICE-01: 4/6 and 6/6 (UNREASONABLE, UNREASONABLE, FAIL)
- CHOICE-02: 6/6 and 6/6 (FAIL, which is a grader false positive, then PASS, UNREASONABLE)
- CHOICE-03: 5/6 and 6/6 (PASS, FAIL, PASS)

## Findings (diagnosed, not fixed)

1. **The quick reply guesses before the normal turn can ask (CHOICE-01 r3 P1).** The quick reply has no tools and is not bound by `AMBIGUITY_RULE`. It decided "改成周四" meant the trip and promised to pass it to the trip Bee. The normal turn then kept that promise ("我上一条回复里说‘会一并交给’它，现在已经真的递过去了") and dispatched instead of showing a card. The card can only win if the quick reply also stays neutral on an ambiguous message.
2. **Recency guess (CHOICE-03 r2 P3).** P2 had just sent a follow-up to the meeting Bee. "时间往后推一天吧" was then steered to that running task, against the rule's "not even the most recent".
3. **Cards without `task_ref` (CHOICE-01 r2 P1, CHOICE-02 r3 P2).** Neither turn called `list_bees`, so every option was a bare label. The Host accepts this: under the contract, an option without `task_ref` is a topic Beebou handled itself. A click on such an option carries only `chosen_note` and no Bee/task binding.
4. **Steer to a `waiting_user` task is denied `not_granted` (CHOICE-01 r1 P1).** In that repeat the trip Bee asked the user a question, so the T3 `bee_terminal` wait timed out (`met: false`) and the setup was not met. P1 tried to steer to the waiting task. The Host action authorizer returned `{"status":"denied","reason":"not_granted"}`, and Beebou told the user that raw reason. A setup wait that times out is not graded as a setup ERROR today. That is existing suite behaviour and unchanged here.
5. **Grader false positive (CHOICE-02 r1 P3).** The reply said "The rota swap is done". That follow-up task was `running` in the before-snapshot and finished during the turn, so Beebou relayed the Bee's real result. `live_normal_no_false_done` only accepts tasks that completed before the turn. The dispatch decision itself was correct. Human judgement should record PASS.

## Checks

- `node tests/eval/hive-live/grade.mjs --validate`: 53 cases valid
- `node tests/eval/hive-live/grade.mjs --catalogue --check`: up to date
- `node --test tests/eval/hive-live.test.mjs`: 46/46 pass
- `python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests/eval/hive-live -p 'test_hive_live_*.py'`: 26 tests OK

1814.author: Jianyu010
1814.body:
Closes #1810

## Problem

On an unreferenced Home follow-up that more than one task could fit ("改成周四" with three candidate tasks), the tool-less quick reply named a target and promised to forward the message. The normal turn then kept that promise and dispatched instead of calling `ask_choice`, which breaks ADR-0026 decision 2 (never guess; ask with a choice card). Evidence: HIVE-LIVE-CHOICE-01 r3 P1, run `1644-choice-4371a5ec`.

## Change (prompt text only, `temp/hive-beebou/src/dm_hive_beebou/config/quick_reply.toml`)

- `[quick] prompt`: when the latest message refers to earlier work without saying which task or topic it means, and more than one could fit, the quick reply does not guess. It names none of them, does not restate the change as applying to one of them, and does not say it will pass the message on. It only acknowledges and says it is checking which one is meant. The example is the same as in `AMBIGUITY_RULE`.
- `[normal] quick_note`: the quick reply ran without tools or `list_bees`, so a task it named is a guess, not a decision. When neither the message nor a system note identifies one task, the normal turn ignores that choice and follows its ambiguity rule as it would without the quick reply. If more than one task fits, it calls `ask_choice` and does not dispatch, even if the quick reply said it would pass the message on.

Not changed: no code, no wire, Store or Host change, and no new entry point. The quick reply still has no tools. The two layers back each other up: (a) keeps the visible quick text honest, and (b) keeps the card even when a model ignores (a).

## Tests

- `temp/hive-beebou/tests/test_beebou_ambiguous_quick_reply.py` (new):
  - checks that the rule text is in both prompts;
  - checks that the neutral acknowledgement passes every quick-reply guard (pending, empty task view, active tasks);
  - checks that the quick request carries the rule and offers no tools;
  - replays the r3 P1 quick text as a published prelude. The normal turn reads the note right after it, its `ask_choice` stands, and there is no promise-guard reprompt.
- `harness/.../tests/test_hive_beebou_choice_card.py::test_a_quick_reply_that_guessed_a_target_never_replaces_the_card` (product entry, controlled model): the follow-up arrives while a turn is busy, and the guessing quick reply is published (`QUICK_COMMITTED`). The normal turn sees the guess and then the note, its card is accepted with both Bee options, and nothing is dispatched.
- Local runs (Python 3.13): `temp/hive-beebou` 152 passed; `temp/hive-runtime` 150 passed / 1 skipped; `tests/scenarios/hive/test_phase2_quick_reply.py` 7 passed; Bridge `tests/test_hive*.py`: see the comment below.

## Live check

HIVE-LIVE-CHOICE-01 with the product model. Results are posted as a comment.

## Docs

- `docs/implementations/contracts/beebou-choice-card.md` C4: new quick-reply paragraph.
- `docs/implementations/contracts/UPDATES.md`: new entry.

1815.author: Jianyu010
1815.body:
Closes #1811

## Problem

In the real-model run `1644-choice-4371a5ec` (`HIVE-LIVE-CHOICE-01` r1):

- **P1.** The trip Bee was waiting on the user's answer (`waiting_user`). The user sent "改成周四。" and Beebou steered that task. The Host refused it with `{"status":"denied","reason":"not_granted"}`, so the correction never reached the Bee. Beebou then told the user "Host 拒绝了这次补充，返回的原因是 not_granted".
- **P4.** A steer to a finished task was refused the same way. Beebou rightly fell back to `new` with `follows`, but still told the user "Host 拒绝了".

## Decision for part 2 (ADR-0027)

**A steer of a `waiting_user` task is allowed, and it is always queued.** This was not a deliberate safety refusal. The #1431 `_UserActionAuthorizer` allowed only `queued` and `running` tasks. Everywhere else a waiting task already counts as open:

- the Store accepts a steer to any task that has not finished;
- the Host-routed send (SC04-C2) steers `waiting_user` with `followup_mode='queue'` (`[routing] steer_states`);
- the choice-card note tells Beebou to steer a waiting task whose question the user's message does not answer.

A supplement cannot settle the Bee's question. Only `answer_bee` can, and only with the user's own words (#1661). So allowing the steer adds no authority beyond steering a running task.

- For a waiting task the dispatch always uses `followup_mode='queue'`, whatever `queues.bee.followup` says. No live steer control is recorded for the parked Run. The Bee reads the supplement after its question is answered.
- The accepted receipt carries the `waiting_supplement` detail. It says the Bee reads the change after the question is answered, tells Beebou to relay the question if it is still open, and tells Beebou not to say the change was applied.
- If the user's message answers the Bee's question, Beebou still uses `answer_bee`.

## Part 1: refusals tell Beebou the next step

- hive-runtime `beebou_tool_grant.py`: the authorizer may return `ActionDenied(detail)`. `DeniedToolResult` adds that detail, or else the turn's default, as `detail`. `status` and `reason` are unchanged.
- The Bridge authorizer gives a detail for each cause: no current user message (for example a Bee report), `source_ids` citing another message, bad arguments, a finished task (use `new` with `follows`), a task that is not this Bee's open task (call `list_bees`), and anything else.
- Beebou's instruction gains `user_facing_rule`: never tell the user about the Host, tool names, IDs, statuses, reasons or codes; when the user needs to know, say the outcome in plain words.
- All wording is in `temp/hive-beebou/src/dm_hive_beebou/config/refusal.toml` (`load_refusal`). A missing, empty or unknown key fails at load time. `beebou-prompt-v1` is unchanged.

Docs: ADR-0027 (plus the ADR index and ADR UPDATES) and `docs/UPDATES.md`.

## Tests

- New in `test_hive_beebou_bee_question.py`:
  - A supplement to a waiting Bee is accepted with the waiting detail under both `queue` and `steer` follow-up modes. It writes one queued supplement and no steer control, and the question stays `OPEN`. The later answer is still settled by `answer_bee`. I checked that the test fails when the authorizer change is reverted (both modes), and when the forced queue is reverted (steer mode: the supplement is lost).
  - A steer of a finished task is denied with the `task_finished` detail, and nothing is written.
  - The instruction carries the rule, and no detail contains `Host` or `not_granted`.
- Updated:
  - grant tests: a specific detail for each cause (`test_hive_beebou_tool_grant.py`); the default detail on a Bee report's turn (`test_hive_bee_induced_reply.py`);
  - `sc03_bees.py` scenario check;
  - the `test_hive_self_steer_guard.py` fake task now has a `state`.
- New in hive-runtime `test_beebou_tool_grant.py` and hive-beebou `test_beebou_refusal_settings.py`.
- Local results:
  - `temp/hive-beebou`: 154 passed.
  - `temp/hive-runtime`: 151 passed, 1 skipped.
  - Bridge `tests/test_hive*.py`: 528 passed, 3 skipped, 7 xfailed. 10 failed, and the same 10 fail on clean `origin/main` `771c28e5` in the same venv (local dependency skew: `test_hive_bee_lifecycle` pre-claim wiring, `test_hive_bee_runtime_local_tools`, `test_hive_bee_unavailable_terminal`, `test_hive_document_model_reads`).

## Live check

Real product model, `tests/eval/hive-live` over `local_cli`, server env built from the wheel at `97ff7aae` (package proof PASS; it includes `refusal.toml`). Three new cases, 2 repeats each. Traces are kept in the shared hive-live artifacts store under `1811-97ff7aae/runs/`.

| Case | What it drives | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| REFUSAL-01 | Bee asks the departure city → "改成周四。" while waiting → answer → later change | P1 steer of the `waiting_user` task **accepted and queued with the `waiting_supplement` detail** in both repeats. Each reply said in plain words that the change was passed on and will apply after the question is answered, and relayed the question. |
| REFUSAL-02 | Same, single question, then the Bee's report | r2: P1 steer accepted and queued with the waiting detail; P2 `answer_bee` settled the question (interaction `ANSWERED`); **the queued supplement is `CONSUMED`**; the Bee's report opens with "已把日期改到 2026-11-26（周四）". r1: Beebou created a new Bee, which finished without asking, so it used `new`+`follows`. |
| REFUSAL-03 | Change to a completed task | Both repeats went straight to `new`+`follows` and gave clean replies. |

- **Internal terms:** none of Host, `not_granted`, `denied`, tool names, `task_ref` or `bee_id` appeared in any user-facing reply, in any repeat.
- **Grader:** the cases are now in `tests/eval/hive-live/regression-cases/1811-refusal.json`, outside the 50-case catalogue, and run with `drive.py --cases-dir`. The first expectations were too strict. P1 now also accepts `new:reuse` for when the Bee finished without asking. P3 also accepts `steer` while the task is still open. P2 counts as weak, not a FAIL, when a multi-part `answer_bee` is refused or there is no question to answer. Regrading the same traces: REFUSAL-03 PASS ×2. REFUSAL-01 UNREASONABLE: r1 sent two steers where one was enough. REFUSAL-02: r2 PASS, r1 ERROR, because its Bee never asked, so no report exists to grade. No FAIL.
- **Existing #1661 gap, not changed here.** In REFUSAL-01 r1 the resumed Bee called `ask_user` again. `BeeAnswerResume.resume` returned `None`, `answer_finisher` raised, and `answer_bee` reported "delivery outcome unknown: RuntimeError". The task stayed open, which is why P3 steered. Filed as #1826 (part of #1665).
- The refused-steer detail path (`task_finished`, `task_unknown` and others) is covered by unit tests. In the live runs, Beebou picked the right route without first being refused.

1816.author: Jianyu010
1816.body:
Refs #1804

The #967 idle release closed the connection about 9 s after a Home send: the send landed near the end of a quiet window, and the Beebou reply push then had no socket to arrive on. This change fixes it in the client connection layer (`DigitalMateClient`).

## Changes

**1. Last-activity semantics for what the user does.**
- A user-started request resets the idle clock when it is sent and again when its response arrives. The user-started requests are `room.message`, `task.create`/`run`/`answer`/`cancel`, `session.steer`/`queue`/`preempt` and `hive.message.send`.
- Self-traffic still never keeps a quiet connection alive: the embedded chat's 3 s `snapshot` poll, `config.get`, `room.home` and history reads. This keeps the #967 intent, and the earlier receipts test is now an explicit self-poll test.

**2. An accepted Beebou Home send whose reply is still awaited counts as busy.**
- Signals that start the wait:
  - The response snapshot has the send's Hive Home user row (`hive-home:<s>:<seq>:user`, matched on `submission_id`) but no `:reply` row yet.
  - `hive.message.send` (a choice click or its fallback) answers `pending` or `accepted`.
  - A Home send times out on the client, so its outcome is unknown and the turn may still be running.
- Signals that end the wait:
  - The matching `hive.beebou.reply` push (`source_message_id`), committed or failed.
  - Any later snapshot that shows the reply row (covers a missed push).
  - A refusal (`accepted: false`).
  - `disconnect()`.
  - The configured bound.
- Sends to an ordinary room (no Hive Home row) start no wait. The injected `isBusy` (running snapshot tasks, from `DigitalMateTaskRuntime`) still covers those, unchanged.
- A named send to a Bee Session (`target_session_ref`) starts no wait. That Bee answers it, not a Beebou push.

**3. The bound comes from config.**
- The bound is `app_config.json` → `digitalmate.replyWaitMs`. The shipped `app_config.example.json` sets 600000 (10 min).
- An installation whose own `app_config.json` predates the key uses the example's value.
- If neither file sets it, no wait is tracked.
- `scripts/sync-app-config.mjs` validates the key: a positive integer.
- There is no numeric default in the client.

## Tests

- `tests/unit/digitalmate-idle-disconnect.test.mjs`: 8 new #1804 cases. All 8 fail on the old client and pass now. They cover:
  - a response resets the clock (the issue timeline);
  - a send alone resets it;
  - a pending Hive reply blocks the idle release;
  - the reply push ends the wait, and a failed push ends it too;
  - another send's push leaves this wait alone;
  - a reply in the response or in a later poll needs no wait;
  - the bound releases the wait;
  - the `hive.message.send` statuses, a refusal and a named Bee send;
  - a timed-out Home send keeps waiting, and a disconnect ends every wait.
- Also added: a config test (no client default; the example sets the bound).
- `tests/unit/digitalmate-config.test.mjs`: the local value wins, the example fallback reads each file once, and an invalid value is ignored.
- `tests/unit/sync-app-config.test.mjs`: `replyWaitMs` validation.
- Full `scripts/ci/node-tests.sh` run locally: 4072/4081 passed before the config-loader fix commit. The fix commit resolves the one product failure, and the three affected files pass (44/44). The remaining failures are Chromium visual tests: this machine has no Playwright browser installed. They are unrelated and run in CI.
- `hvigorw assembleHap`: ArkTS compiles with no errors.

## Device

The emulator repro ran locally on a Pura 90 emulator, with an unsigned HAP built from head `54f57889` and installed with `install -r`. The account's real Gateway was the backend.

**PASS:**

| Time | Event |
| --- | --- |
| 13:18:15.4 | `handshake_ok` |
| 13:18:15 to 13:23:05 | Quiet, app in the foreground |
| 13:23:05 | Home send (4:50 into the quiet window) |
| ~13:23:17 | The reply is on screen |
| 13:23:15 | The old deadline passes; the connection stays open, with no `idle_release` |
| 13:28:40.4 | `idle_release {"elapsedMs":300002}`, exactly one idle window after the last activity (13:23:40) |

So the issue's "9 s after a send" release no longer happens, and the release follows last-activity semantics.

Limitations:
- This account's Home is an ordinary DigitalMate room (`msg-*` rows), not a Beebou Hive Home. The Hive "awaiting reply" path (a reply arriving more than 5 min after the send) was exercised by the unit tests above, not on the device.
- An earlier attempt at 12:51–12:57 was invalid: another app took the foreground mid-run. It is not counted.

1818.body:
Refs #1648 #1665

## What

This is the Phase 0 design PR for #1648. It lands the D6 resumable-helper design on `main`. The design draft and review deck that the issue body links to exist only at `e7bbc16c`, which never reached `main` (bot F4).

| Piece | File |
| --- | --- |
| Versioned specification v1 (D-BH-01–09, S-BH-01–05, C-BH-01–03, T6.1–T6.3) | `docs/implementations/contracts/hive-browser-helper-1648.md` |
| Architecture review deck v1 (from `architecture-change-review-template.pptx`, same IDs) | `docs/assets/feature-design/hive-browser-helper-review-v1.pptx` |
| Acceptance record | `docs/implementations/adrs/0028-hive-resumable-browser-helper.md` (0027 is taken by #1815) |
| Index and update entries | contracts, feature-design and ADR `README.md` / `UPDATES.md` |
| JiuwenBox docstring fix (bot F2), recorded as an import override; IDs recomputed with `update_upstream_ids.py` | `harness/workswarm/jiuwenbox/src/jiuwenbox/server/sandbox_manager.py`, `harness/UPSTREAM.json` |

The stale #1533 pointer is replaced by #1665 throughout (bot F6).

## Owner decisions

I am the v3.1 lead, deciding here for Host Runtime, Browser / Sandbox and Session Store. Each decision's rationale is in the spec.

- **D-BH-01 First workflow.** `python-docs-two-page` reads two fixed public pages in order: `docs.python.org/3/library/json.html` and `.../tomllib.html`. The model supplies only the workflow ID. Results carry each page's `source_id`, content sha256 and a checkable marker.
- **D-BH-02 Runtime.** A task-scoped helper process runs its steps through the product `PageFetcher`, which only connects to public addresses and bounds redirects and response size.
  - Playwright `browser_agent` is not used. It is switched off on the server, and the image has no Chromium or Node.
  - JiuwenBox is not used. It is not deployed, it cannot run in a non-root gVisor Pod, and its registry is ephemeral.
- **D-BH-03 Identity.** The helper is bound to principal, task, Bee, Session, Run, run generation, operation and workflow.
  - The operation ID is the gate's persisted `bee-effect:<run>:<gen>:<step>:<call>`.
  - `helper_key` is the sha256 of that binding.
  - A new Run never resumes an old checkpoint.
- **D-BH-04 Checkpoint.**
  - The helper runtime writes the confirmed steps, their excerpts and the references needed to resume.
  - The Host holds the permission, which is never stored in the checkpoint.
  - The Store holds the Hive job and the receipts: the effect plan and its result.
- **D-BH-05 Retention.** A checkpoint is deleted once its plan settles, immediately on Stop or revoke, after a configured maximum age, and on principal erasure. A content-free tombstone answers `lookup`.
- **D-BH-06 Lifecycle.**
  - Cold start runs a separate process group with an allowlisted environment and a handshake.
  - Sleep means the process exits when idle.
  - Close sends `close`, then SIGKILL.
  - A single-holder lease is taken per key, and resumes are bounded.
  - All values are in TOML.
- **D-BH-07 Recovery boundary.**
  - The Host re-checks the Run and Session binding, the public-read authorization, any Stop reservation and the feature switch before every start, every step and every disclosure.
  - The runtime re-checks that the binding equals the checkpoint and that path and lease isolation hold.
  - Stop revokes continuation.
  - Unknown outcomes are reconciled by the original ID; `lookup` never executes a step.
- **D-BH-08 Enablement.** Off by default. `DIGITALMATE_HIVE_BROWSER_HELPER=1` turns it on for the ordinary product composition only. It does not change the Harness identity.
- **D-BH-09 Acceptance.** Targeted local tests and CI, plus runtime-gated tests on the HK runtime host with `WORKSWARM_RUNTIME_TESTS=1`. A direct QA instance runs in a dedicated test cluster namespace, never the shared test environment.

## Boundary with #1675

After a Host process restart, the original Bee Run cannot be re-entered: the entry fence, `persist_session=False` and the #1655 orphan rule prevent it. In that case:

- The helper reconciles its plan by the original key; it does not replay.
- Continuing that Run, so the result still reaches Home through the original Bee, is #1675's `persist_session` / `history.jsonl` scope. This PR does not change it.
- Once #1675 accepts Run continuation, the same operation ID maps to the same `helper_key` and resumes from its checkpoint.

Within one Bee call, sandbox close, sleep and helper-process restart (SIGKILL, empty registry) all resume transparently.

Refs #1788 #1749

Closes the Global Memory gap left by #1802: Beebou and granted Bees can now read the owner's Hive Global Memory through the existing `native_search_memory` / `native_read_memory` tools.

## What changes
- **Grant rule** (`dm_hive_tools/handlers/memory_ports.py` `GlobalMemoryGrants`, defaults in `config/global_memory.toml`):
  - Beebou: granted by default (`beebou_default = true`) for its own principal.
  - Bee: granted only when the Beebou `dispatch` (mode new) that created the task carries `global_memory_read: true`. The Host records it after the Store accepts the dispatch (`hive_beebou_tools._EffectFencedBotTools`). When the dispatch leaves the flag out, `bee_dispatch_default = false` applies. `dm_beebou` `dispatch` accepts the optional boolean on new only.
  - `revoke_task` / `revoke_owner` remove a grant. The next read returns nothing, and a revoke during a read discloses nothing (the grant is re-checked before disclosure).
  - Grants live in process. After a restart a Bee task holds none (fail closed).
- **Scope**: owner principal only. `scope_for` returns the engine principal's own scope, or None for any other principal or room. Refusals use the same "nothing" text as an empty result.
- **Results**: Global matches are merged with Local ones, ranked by query-word overlap and then by each source's own order. They are labelled `source = "global"` and `scope.reach = "global"`, carry `provenance` (source_key, source_rev, locator, role, author, occurred_at_ms, memory_rev), and use the id `global:<memory_id>`, which `native_read_memory` reads under the same grant. `include_global: false` leaves Global Memory out.
- **Wiring**: `hive_memory_services(..., global_memory=configured_global_memory(engine.path))` in server.py. The port and grants are injected only when `dm_hive_memory/config/live.toml` `provider_directory` is non-empty. Without a provider, an explicit Global read (`include_global: true` or a `global:` id) is refused with "Global Memory is unavailable." A default search returns Local results only. The services reach both `register_hive_tools` (Beebou) and `bee_host_tools` (Bee).
- **No writes**: reads call only `GlobalMemoryProvider.retrieve`, which reads the surface twice and refuses if `surface_rev` moved in between (approach from draft #1750 by huben0423-hw, credited). A test hashes every `hm_*` row before and after reads.
- **No new tool name**: the existing rows are extended, so the catalog is unchanged.
- **Packaging**: no new package path. The new files sit inside `dm_hive_tools`, which the wheel and the Dockerfile already ship.

Fixes #1674.

## Problem
`HiveBeebouModel.context_message` dropped OpenAI's deprecated `function_call` along with the provider's other extra fields. Reproduced on 498bc351:
- **Quick reply:** committed the text beside the call (`我查一下。`).
- **Normal turn:** committed that prose as the final answer and never ran the tool the model asked for.

## Decision
Convert `function_call` in the adapter rather than reject it or retry:
- With `tools` offered, which is the only way Beebou asks, no served model sends `function_call` (probe below). Handling it is insurance, not a hot path.
- The realistic way it could start is a gateway that maps `tools` to the legacy format. That would happen on every call, so reject-and-retry would fail all its retries on every tool turn. Converting handles that case on the first try. It needs no new setting and no new user-facing message.

  - A repeated id in one context is renamed by the Harness's existing `unique_call_ids`.
  - When `tool_calls` is also present, `function_call` is dropped.
  - Each conversion logs one warning.
- Resulting behaviour:
  - Quick reply refuses it as `tool_request` (before: committed the text, or `empty` when the call came alone).
  - Second quick and normal turns run it through the Host grant gate.
- Tests:

Delivers the #1675 evaluation: a decision record for Bee full-context persistence and restart recovery, one runtime fix the validation matrix found, and the tests that execute the matrix.

## Decision record

[`docs/implementations/contracts/hive-bee-context-recovery.md`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/DigitalMate/blob/claude/hive-1675-bee-context-e6b4d0/docs/implementations/contracts/hive-bee-context-recovery.md) (ACCEPTED, owner Jianyu010):

- **D1** The authoritative Bee transcript is the WorkSwarm runtime Session's `history.jsonl`. `warmup_session_context` rebuilds the in-memory context from it after a restart, a `session.unload` + `acquire_runtime` re-attach, or idle adapter eviction.
- **D2** The Session Store does not own a full transcript. `dm_hive_bee_contexts` keeps the #1491 per-turn witnesses. The doc lists each failure considered and why a witness, the history or neither covers it.
- **D3** `context_ref` is committed when the Store row and the input consumption commit in one transaction. After a lost ACK, replaying the same `(run_id, turn)` and digest is safe. Any other replay is refused.
- **D4** A pre-execution Stop checkpoint is not a committed state. Only the witnessed `kind='stopped'` record commits.
- **D5 (fix)** see below.
- **D6** Retention: restart and unload keep the history; the Bee runtime owner `WorkSwarmAdapter` deletes the history of retired or superseded Sessions. That work is filed as #1819 under #1665.
- **D7** Close draft #1504 without merging or extracting it. The matrix re-covers its acceptance intent on the current contract.

## Fix: the completion proof waits for the Session history

The runtime writes `history.jsonl` through one asynchronous FIFO writer. The Host commits a turn's Store context as soon as `session.runtime_state` reports `COMPLETED`. A runtime killed between those two points rebuilt the next turn without the reply the Store had already committed.

`SessionUnloadController.completion` and `resume_completion` (`deploy/runtime_patches/session_unload.py`) now place a history barrier (`RuntimeUnloadPorts.history_written`, which calls `session_history.flush_pending_writes`) before they report `COMPLETED`. Until it passes they report `BUSY`. The barrier reuses the controller's existing `timeout`. There is no Store, wire or config change.

Phase 1 (T6.1) of #1648: the resumable browser helper for Hive Bees, per the design on main ([contract](docs/implementations/contracts/hive-browser-helper-1648.md) D-BH-01–09, ADR-0028). Off by default.

## What it does

A Bee in a Home task can call `hive_browser_helper {"workflow": "python-docs-two-page"}`. The Host admits it as a journaled bound effect of the Bee effect gate (PLANNED before anything runs, EXECUTED is the receipt). The provider then:

- binds the job to the lane the Host opened (principal, task, Bee Session, Run, generation, operation ID); model arguments choose only the workflow ID, never pages;
- runs one helper process per helper key, one step per request, and commits each confirmed step to the Browser / Sandbox checkpoint before replying;
- asks `BeeEffectGate.permitted` before every cold start, every step and the disclosure, so a Stop or revocation stops the job, revokes its checkpoint and discloses nothing;
- if the process closes, sleeps, dies or loses a reply, cold-starts again under the same key (bounded by `max_resumes` and `call_budget_ms`) and continues from the checkpoint; a confirmed step is never read twice;
- answers `lookup(operation_id)` from the checkpoint or tombstone only (reconciliation without replay), and sweeps settled or over-age checkpoints.

The result goes back to Home through the original Bee: it is the tool result of the Bee's own call.

## Changes

- `temp/hive-browser-helper` (new feature, own `ownership.json`): settings and `browser_helper.toml`, binding, checkpoint store, helper process protocol, sandbox client, provider, README, tests.
- `BeeEffectGate.permitted` (`temp/hive-runtime`): the lane's current grant for a running bound effect.
- Bridge: `server_engine/hive_browser_helper.py` (process entry with the product page reader), composition in `compose_bee_runtime` (ordinary product path only, switch `DIGITALMATE_HIVE_BROWSER_HELPER` or `[feature] enabled`), wheel force-include, Dockerfile and build context.
- CI: `ci-gates.json` enrolment (`hive-browser-helper`, 38 tests) and active capture bound.
- `tests/server/test_installed_package_proof.py`: adds `hive-tools` (missing on main, so two of its tests fail on main today) and `hive-browser-helper` to the transition tables.

## Tests

- Component (real helper subprocesses; only the page fetch is substituted): checkpoint, binding and settings; process protocol (cold start, close, sleep, kill during a step, lost reply after commit, failed step, isolation re-check, one process per key, revoke, environment allowlist); provider (resume after close, sleep, lost reply, Host process restart, resume limit, Stop between steps and during the last step, cancellation, revocation before the first step, cross-tenant lane and lookup, model arguments, page injection, concurrent resume, retention sweep, erasure).
- Gate: `test_permitted_rechecks_the_lane_for_a_running_bound_effect`.
- Bridge: `tests/test_hive_browser_helper_bridge.py` (off by default, one bound effect when on, real process entry handshake).
- Real runtime: `tests/scenarios/hive/test_home_bee_browser_helper.py` with `WORKSWARM_RUNTIME_TESTS=1` (live two-page case with `HIVE_LIVE_PUBLIC_PAGE_TEST=1`; lost reply plus sleep resume; Stop; switch off).

**B5: the first model call missed `todo_*` / `skill_tool`.** This was not an ordering problem. The first model call (and the first after a resume) runs before WorkSwarm writes its session key into `ctx.extra`, so `HostAskOnlyRail` asked the Host gate for lane `None` and got only the ask-only set.
- The rail now falls back to `ctx.session.get_session_id()`.
- If both ids are present and disagree, the rail exposes nothing.
- The rail's exposure filter now runs last in `before_model_call`.

**B6: every Host tool failed after an `ask_user` answer.** `run_turn` releases the gate lane when a turn pauses on `ask_user`, and `BeeAnswerResume` never bound it again. The resume now rebinds the exact lane from the Store's Run runtime record (`read_bee_run_runtime`), which must match on:
- the same runtime Session;
- the same runtime generation (checked against the adapter token);
- the same persisted binding;
- the asking turn's `run_turn`, so the continued agent-core iteration maps to the same effect plan key.

Any mismatch binds nothing, and calls then get `no_active_run`. Another Run's lane is never displaced, and the lane is released after the resume.

**Usability (§10.3)**
1. **Paths.** Absolute paths under the runtime cwd/workspace map to task-relative paths (longest root first, the root itself → `.`). A configurable per-turn note (`dm_hive_tools/config/bee_prompt.toml`; empty turns it off) is appended after the user's text and asks for task-relative paths. It names no Host path. I did not re-point the WorkSwarm workspace, because runtime Sessions are reused across Tasks and the system prompt is fixed when the agent is created.
2. **Empty Tasks.** `prepare_lane` creates the task work dir when the lane is bound, so a Task with no files lists as empty.
3. **Refusal classes.** Read refusals return `Document unavailable (<class>).` with `{"status":"refused","reason":<class>}`, where the class is one of `outside_workspace`, `not_found`, `no_active_run` or `unavailable_on_host`. The message never includes file content, Host paths or other Task names.
4. **Delivery name.** Delivery is exposed as `deliver_file`. If the runtime registered only `send_file_to_user`, the call is renamed back to that alias for later runtime rails. It still goes through the Host gate, and the runtime never executes it.

The design record is §8 of `docs/implementations/contracts/hive-tool-access-1749.md`.

## Tests

- **B5 and B6 on the real patched WorkSwarm runtime:** `test_hive_bee_lane_real.py` (`WORKSWARM_RUNTIME_TESTS=1`) streams a turn that asks `ask_user`, then resumes it.
  - The first model call already has the `todo_*` tools.
  - Every call, including those after the resume, sees the same set, with `deliver_file` present and `send_file_to_user` absent.
  - After the resume, a read through the absolute runtime cwd path returns the file.
  - The resumed calls return `(not_found)` and `(outside_workspace)` refusal classes; neither "No running Bee Run is bound" nor the ask-only refusal appears.
- **B6 lane identity:** `test_bee_answer_lane.py` covers:
  - the exact turn, read, journaled effect and lane after a resume;
  - the claim turn resuming as turn 0;
  - no lane on a generation, session or turn mismatch;
  - a changed binding being refused;
  - another Run never being displaced.
- **Usability:** `test_hive_bee_tool_usability.py` (empty Task, refusal classes, `no_active_run` / `unavailable_on_host`, cwd mapping, `deliver_file` exposure and alias, rail priority, note config), the new missing-session-key cases in `test_hive_bee_runtime_local_tools.py`, and the refusal classes in `test_hive_tools_workspace.py`.

1838.author: Jianyu010
1838.body:
## Problem

Every `pr-ready.yml` run shared one concurrency group, `pr-ready-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}`, with `cancel-in-progress: true`. A `labeled`/`unlabeled` event for an unrelated label creates a run whose jobs all skip, but that run still joins the group and cancels the in-progress ST.

Evidence from #1824:
- 06:31:14Z — `pr-ready` added, run 44031820774 started `st`, which was then **cancelled**.
- 06:31:16–17Z — `agent-ci-infra-bot` added `backend`, `bot-reviewed`, `bug` and `priority:P1`. Each label event produced a run that skipped or was cancelled, and the first of them cancelled the ST.

The header comment also claimed that unrelated labels "do not restart or cancel the ST", which was wrong.

## Fix

```yaml
group: pr-ready-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}-${{ (github.event.action == 'labeled' || github.event.action == 'unlabeled') && github.event.label.name != 'pr-ready' && github.run_id || 'gate' }}
cancel-in-progress: true
```

- `labeled`/`unlabeled` with any label other than `pr-ready` → suffix is the run's own `run_id`, a group nobody else joins, so it has nothing to cancel (and cannot replace a pending run either).
- Every other event (`opened`, `synchronize`, `reopened`, `ready_for_review`, `pr-ready` labeled/unlabeled) → suffix `gate`, the shared group, so a new commit or a `pr-ready` change still restarts the ST as before.
- Job `if:` conditions are unchanged; the header and concurrency comments now describe the real behaviour.

## Verification

- **Expression trace** (`tests/unit/ci-gate.test.mjs`, new tests): the actual `group`/`cancel-in-progress` strings are read from `pr-ready.yml` and evaluated per event shape:
  - `synchronize` (two runs), `opened`, `reopened`, `ready_for_review`, `labeled pr-ready` and `unlabeled pr-ready` all resolve to `pr-ready-pr-ready-1824-gate`.
  - A different PR number gets a different group.
  - The #1824 bot labels (`backend`, `bot-reviewed`, `bug`, `priority:P1`), labeled and unlabeled, each resolve to a unique group that is never the ST group.
- **Mutation checks**: the pre-fix shared group, a constant instead of `run_id`, an inverted label test, dropping the `unlabeled` branch, a per-run shared group and `cancel-in-progress: false` each make the behaviour test fail.
- `node --test tests/unit/ci-gate.test.mjs`: 22/22 pass. `actionlint` reports only the existing custom runner-label warnings.
- Live check: `pull_request_target` always runs the workflow from `main`, so this PR's own runs still use the old group. The fix can only be seen live on PRs labelled after this merges.

Refs #1841 #1783 #1749

## What

Beebou's catalog reads now check the Session Store at the same two points as Bee reads through the Host effect gate:

- **Before execution:** the Store must still show Beebou's binding as current. A revoked, rebound or stopped session is refused before the Gateway runs, and nothing is returned.
- **Before disclosure:** the binding is read again. If it changed while the read ran, the result is discarded.

## Where

- `server_engine/hive_beebou_agentcore.py`: `_GatewayReadTool.current()` / `call()`. This is the Host provider that sends every Beebou catalog tool into `PluginGateway`: `agentcore-tools` (file, grep, PDF, attachment and memory reads) and `agentcore-skills` (`skill_tool`).
- `server_engine/hive_turn_startup.py`:
  - **Normal turn:** `bind_tools` gives the Run its own fenced copies. They read `read_beebou_context_binding(scope, session_ref, generation, source_seq, run_id)`, the existing Store read the native runner and Home to-dos already use. It returns a binding only while the context claim is RUNNING and the Beebou bot binding is ACTIVE for that session and generation, so it covers revoke, rebind and Stop.
  - **Quick phases** (no claim yet): the fence is `read_bot_binding`, which requires ACTIVE status and the same session_ref and generation.
- `dm_hive_runtime/assembly/turn_grants.py`: `ReviewedReadOnlyTools` re-runs a fenced provider's `current()` before it reuses material prepared by the second quick phase. Without this, a read prepared before Stop could be shown afterwards.

No new store, table or schema.

## Refusal classes

These use the Bee read path's names from #1833:

- `no_active_run`: the claim or binding is gone, or changed during the read.
- `unavailable_on_host`: no fence is wired, or the Store read failed.

A refusal is a `BeebouToolRefused("FORBIDDEN", "<tool> unavailable (<class>); nothing was read.")` and carries no content.

## Tests

New tests are in `tests/test_hive_beebou_agentcore.py::BeebouStoreFenceTests`. Each case below has its own test:

- revoke between turns
- revoke during a read (result discarded)
- binding revision change during a read
- rebind to another session
- Stop, including reused second-quick material
- forged identity in arguments is ignored (BAD_PARAMS; the fence uses only Host coordinates)
- Store fault or missing fence (`unavailable_on_host`)
- every Gateway tool in a Run is fenced
- the normal read still works (and the quick phase reads through the Session fence)

1848.body:
Refs #1789 #1749 #1790

## Root cause (environmental, proven from my own probe Pod in the HK test namespace)
- Cluster DNS answers `api.open-meteo.com` with a single address (`51.81.167.44`, 12/12 queries). It accepts the TCP SYN and then drops the ClientHello: TLS never answers (TLS1.2-only and other SNI behave the same; the geocoding host and `188.40.99.226`, a second address for the same name, complete TLS in under 1 s).
- No proxy variables in the image; IPv6 is not involved (the API host has no AAAA); the connect budget is not too short.
- So no fetcher change can recover it without bypassing the cluster resolver, which this PR does not do (SSRF/address checks untouched).

## Code defect found on the way
After the TCP probe passed, aiohttp's own TCP+TLS handshake ran while the phase was still `connect`, so the stall was reported as `timeout`/`connect` and looked like an unreachable host. It is now `handshake`, a pre-request phase (no request byte sent, so provably not executed). `response_headers`/`body` timeouts stay unknown and are never re-executed.

## Tests
- `test_a_silent_tls_handshake_is_a_handshake_timeout_not_a_connect_timeout`: a local server accepts TCP and stays silent; asserts `timeout`/`handshake`.
- weather log test for `phase=handshake`.
- 63 passed (engine_watch, engine_weather, weather_mcp) on the remote build host.

## Real network
Fixed code in the probe Pod: `weather_lookup_failed stage=forecast category=timeout phase=handshake` (was `phase=connect`). Probe Pod deleted.

## Follow-up (not here)
`BeeEffectGate` treats any provider exception as an unknown outcome, so this pre-request failure still leaves the plan PLANNED. Mapping it to a known failure belongs to the Hive effect gate. The cluster DNS answer for `api.open-meteo.com` needs an environment fix. Evidence: `docs/verification/records/native-weather-forecast-timeout-1789-20261117.md`.

## Cause

Beebou's normal-turn instruction opened with "Answer directly when appropriate. When Bee work is needed, …" and never said what needs a Bee. To the product model, a grocery list or rota it can write in one reply looks "appropriate", so the T1 decision was a coin flip. T2 and T3 then followed T1 in every repeat of both earlier runs: either all three setups went to Bees or none did.

#1788's `global_memory_read` field on `dispatch` is **not** the cause; see the A/B below.

## Decision ([ADR-0029](docs/implementations/adrs/0029-hive-beebou-delegation-rule.md))

- A piece of work the user may come back to change (a list, plan, schedule, itinerary, agenda, rota, budget, document, report, comparison or code, above all one with several parts) goes to a Bee, even when one reply could hold it. Beebou does not write the work in its own reply. The Bee keeps it as a task that later follow-ups and choice cards can name.
- Short replies stay with Beebou: small talk, facts, arithmetic, rewriting a sentence or two, one-line wishes, questions about earlier work or Bees, read-only tool lookups. This matches the `DECIDE-*`/`SMALL-03` cases.
- New topic, new Bee. Beebou reuses an active Bee only when the request continues its topic.
- The eval cases are unchanged. The choice-card setups and probes are not weakened.

## Change

- `temp/hive-beebou/src/dm_hive_beebou/config/delegation.toml`: `[delegation] rule`, loaded by `load_delegation` (strict: missing, empty or unknown keys fail, no code fallback), now opens `BEEBOU_INSTRUCTION`. The rule's wording is no longer in code. The registry identity `beebou-prompt-v1` is unchanged.
- Docs: ADR-0029, delivery design C11 and §5 (zh and en), and the contracts, ADR and top-level UPDATES logs.
- Tests: `temp/hive-beebou/tests/test_beebou_delegation_settings.py` (4) and `test_instruction_opens_with_the_configured_delegation_rule` (Bridge).

- `tests/scenarios/hive`: 34 failed or erroring, the same set as clean main (local import errors).

## A/B (setup T1 only, product model, `local_cli`)

In every repeat of the two earlier runs, T2 and T3 followed T1, so T1 alone decides whether a repeat reaches the probes. The A/B ran the three cases' T1 (unchanged text) plus a "thanks" filler turn, 8 repeats per case (24 per side), with the same model (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017) and `probe_model.py` go before each side.

1855.body:
Closes #1847

## Cause (trace + Store rows, run `1817-e997cc1f`, `HIVE-LIVE-CHOICE-03` r2 T2)

| ms (…896xxx) | Event |
|---|---|
| 063429 | The `bee_done` turn for seq 3 (birthday list) starts |
| 066570 | User T2 (seq 4) arrives, `busy: true` |
| 071853 | T2 quick reply is published (`hive.reply`). It promises: "之前那份生日会采购清单…有结果回来了，我稍后一并整理给你" |
| 074367 | The seq 3 relay commits (`hive.beebou.reply`, `bee_done`, `committed`) |
| 074373 | The T2 normal turn starts |
| 088855 | The T2 reply says "更正…生日会采购清单的结果我还没有转给你" |

`dm_hive_beebou_context_runs` seq 4 shows exactly what the normal turn saw:

- [8] the `bee_done` report, then [9] the committed relay;
- [10] the user's T2 message, [11] the quick reply, [12] `quick_note`;
- `list_bees`: `results: []`, and `finished[]` with the birthday task `completed`, with nothing saying it had been reported.

Answers to the issue's questions:

1. **Was the view stale?** No. The relay was in context and `results[]` was empty. But `finished[]` gave no explicit delivered flag.
2. **Why the "correction"?** `quick_note` said a quick-reply promise "has NOT been done … correct it and say plainly what has not been done yet". The relay sits above the user's message, although the user saw it after the quick reply. So the promise looked open, and the model "corrected" it.
3. **Was an undisplayed quick reply fed back?** It had been shown. `displayed: false` is the device acknowledgement (`hive.reply.displayed`), which the `local_cli` driver never sends. The quick reply was pushed as a `hive.reply` frame.

## Fix ([ADR-0030](docs/implementations/adrs/0030-hive-beebou-relayed-result-is-delivered.md))

- **Store/Host view:** `list_bees` `finished[]` gains `reported` (boolean). It is true when a committed Beebou context holds the task's `done` report, which is the same consumption that keeps a result out of `results[]` (`recent_finished_tasks`, read only). The `list_bees` description names the field.
- **Config wording (`quick_reply.toml`):**
  - `[normal] quick_note`: a result relayed by a committed `bee_done` turn, or `finished[]` `reported: true`, is delivered wherever the relay sits. The quick reply's promise to pass it on is kept: the normal turn does not correct it and never says "not sent".
  - `[quick] prompt`: the quick reply does not raise Bee results or tasks the message does not ask about.
- **Grader:** `live_normal_no_false_done` attributes a completion claim to the task its sentence names last before the claim. The task's topic terms are its dispatch texts and Bee name, minus the terms the turn's own request shares. A claim about another task holds when that task is completed by the turn's end; every other claim is judged as before (`claim_topic_*` in `hive-live.toml`). The three false flags cited in the issue now pass: `1817-e997cc1f` 03 r2 T2, and `1817-b7bf2e96` 01 r1 P4 and 03 r1 P4.
- Contract `beebou-choice-card.md` C1/C4, contracts/ADR/docs `UPDATES.md`.

## Tests

- New Bridge regression test `test_a_result_relayed_during_the_next_turn_is_reported_in_its_view` reproduces the ordering with a controlled model:
  - it holds the relay turn, sends the next request, lets its quick reply promise the result, then releases;
  - it checks that the normal turn reads the relay before the user's message, then the promise and the note;
  - it checks that `finished[]` reports `false` while the relay runs and `true` after it commits.

  Before the config change it failed on the note.
- `test_hive_beebou_choice_card.py` 18 passed; `temp/hive-beebou/tests` 162 passed; `node --test tests/eval/hive-live.test.mjs` 48 passed, including the new grader test.
- Bridge Hive/Beebou/quick files (local, openjiuwen venv): 556 passed, 10 failed. The same 10 fail on clean main `53674277` (bee lifecycle/unavailable-terminal/document reads/local tools, environment).

## Live evidence

Run `1847-f20c4c11`: `HIVE-LIVE-CHOICE-01/02/03` ×3 at the PR head `f20c4c11`, product model, `local_cli`. The probe passed (all calls 200, p50 6.2 s). 241 model calls; provider errors 0, degraded 0.

| Case | r1 / r2 / r3 | Note |
|---|---|---|
| CHOICE-01 | UNREASONABLE ×3 | T1 setup answered inline (#1845, PR #1851), so the later turns are ungraded |
| CHOICE-02 | UNREASONABLE ×3 | same |
| CHOICE-03 | FAIL ×3 | P3 only; every other turn PASS (see below) |

- **No false "not sent" or "correction" claims.** All 9 repeats were scanned, every normal and quick reply (还没转 / 尚未 / 更正 / 纠正 / not sent / correction): 0 hits.
- **The race was exercised.** In CHOICE-03 r2, T3 and P4 each had a quick reply published, then a `bee_done` relay committed, then the normal reply. Neither quick reply raised the other task's result, and neither normal reply claimed anything was unsent.
- **The `reported` view in the live Store** (r2 context runs): every relayed task shows `reported: true`, and a task still in `results[]` shows `false`, in every `list_bees` call.
- **No regression in the choice-card cases (CHOICE-03):**
  - P1 (ambiguous) gave a card with all three task_refs in 3/3;
  - P2 and P4 (clear follow-ups) went to the right Bee in 3/3;
  - T1–T3 dispatched new Bees in 3/3.
- **P3 FAIL ×3 is pre-existing**, filed as #1859. The prompt "时间往后推一天吧。" right after a clear agenda follow-up was dispatched to the agenda Bee instead of a card. Earlier runs did the same in 4/6 repeats (`1817-e997cc1f`, `1817-b7bf2e96`). P3 had no quick reply, so neither changed config text was on its path.
- The grader change does not touch these verdicts: no turn in this run hit `live_normal_no_false_done`.

Artifacts are kept locally outside the repo: `hive-live-artifacts/1847-f20c4c11/` (`report.md`, `grades.json`, `turns.txt`, traces, Store files).

1860.author: Jianyu010
1860.body:
Fixes #1819 (under #1665; follow-up of #1675).

## What

A Bee's conversation lives in its WorkSwarm runtime Session's `history.jsonl`. Sessions that no scope mapping can reach again (retired / evicted Bee, Session superseded after a preempt or a failed turn) were never deleted. Now they are deleted through WorkSwarm's own `session.delete` after a configured retention.

- **Owner: `WorkSwarmAdapter`** (sole writer of the scope mapping).
  - `_create` records every Session a scope stops naming in a durable ledger `bee-workswarm/history-retention.json` *before* the mapping moves (the mapping keeps one predecessor; the ledger keeps all).
  - `sweep_runtime_history(lanes, retention_seconds, now, delete_timeout_s)` deletes a Session only when: no current mapping names it; its lane is retired or its scope's successor is `ready`; the lane has no RUNNING Run and no OPEN question; nothing in this process holds it; retention has passed since a sweep first saw it eligible.
  - Crash safety: each delete is re-checked and runs under `open_lock` (the fence every mapping change takes); intent `state='deleting'` is durable first; timeouts, connection loss and refusals keep the intent and the next pass repeats it without waiting for retention. A retired scope becomes `state='retired'` and never reopens.
  - Restart, `session.unload` + `acquire_runtime` and idle eviction delete nothing.
- **Store facts:** `HiveStore.bee_session_retention(scope)`. A lane counts as retired only after its slot release witness (no `CLAIMED` eviction). Busy = RUNNING/unwitnessed Run or OPEN question.
- **Host sweep:** `server_engine/hive_bee_history_retention.py`. It runs at startup and then on an interval, with the same lifecycle as slot release, and `engine_cli serve --hive-bees` wires it. Config is in `hive_bee_history_retention.toml` (`after_unreachable_seconds = 86400`, same as #1679; `sweep_interval_seconds = 300`; `delete_timeout_seconds = 60`). It is registered in `temp/hive-worker/ownership.json`; the architecture scan is clean locally.
- Decision record §8 / §8.1 updated: `docs/implementations/contracts/hive-bee-context-recovery.md`.

## Tests

- `agent_bridge/tests/test_workswarm_history_retention.py` (fast, 15): adapter sweep with a controlled Gateway. Covers retention timing, multi-rotation ledger, successor-not-ready, retired lane plus isolation, busy/unknown/held lanes, restart/unload, an interrupted delete (lost answer and cancelled pass) completing after restart, refused delete retried, non-durable mapping, damaged ledger, and an ordinary adapter untouched. The real SQLite Store facts are also tested: busy while RUNNING, and retired only after the release witness.
- `tests/scenarios/hive/test_bee_history_retention.py` (real owned Bee runtime, `WORKSWARM_RUNTIME_TESTS=1`): a retired Bee's history is gone after retention, and the live Bee survives unload and a process restart with its context. A superseded Session's history is gone while its successor keeps working. A sweep whose runtime is SIGKILLed mid-delete finishes on the next pass. No other Bee's Session is touched.

HK evidence is posted on #1819.

Observation, out of scope: the runtime's own logs (`process.log`, `.jiuwenswarm/logs/server.log`) can carry turn text; they are not Session data and are not covered by this sweep.

1861.author: Jianyu010
1861.body:
Fixes #1827 — item (2), `test_workswarm_resume_completion.py` returning `BUSY` instead of `COMPLETED`. Items (1), (3) and (4) landed in #1857.

## Verdict: product defect (a runtime race), not a stale test

Instrumented gated run on the pinned runtime (`verify_installed_unload()` OK):

- at `test_workswarm_resume_completion.py:74-79` the control was `SUCCEEDED`, `cleanup_complete=True`; the parent `chat_stream` was `WAITING_FOR_CONTROL`, `cleanup_complete=True`. The false `completed_resume` check is **`parent.state.terminal`**.
- `busy()` was also true, because the parent is a non-terminal execution; `history_written` was true.

A registry trace of a failing run shows the order:

```
mark_awaiting_control chat_stream  running -> running(q)          # question published
stream_bee returned ['ask_user']                                   # adapter sees the question
mark_running         control_input  -> running                     # answer arrives: parent still RUNNING
mark_waiting         chat_stream    running(q) -> waiting(q)       # original producer parks only now
mark_terminal        control_input  -> succeeded                   # parent left waiting, id cleared
```

In the pinned `RuntimeSessionCoordinator.deliver_control_stream`, the parent is settled only when it was already `WAITING_FOR_CONTROL` when the answer arrived (`parent_was_waiting`). Otherwise the control just clears `parent.waiting_control_id`. When the producer parks the parent *during* the control, the parent stays `WAITING_FOR_CONTROL` with no control id until the Session closes. `resume_completion` then reports `BUSY` forever. In passing runs the producer parks first. The unary `deliver_control` already handles this race with `parent_finished_while_delivering`; the streamed path did not.

## Change

- `deploy/runtime_patches/workswarm-session-unload.json`: a fourth `session/coordinator.py` replacement. After a successful streamed answer, it also settles a parent that is `WAITING_FOR_CONTROL` for this exact control id. This mirrors the unary path. A parent parked for a *different* (newer) question is untouched. `after_sha256` is updated and verified against `harness/workswarm` (the upstream copy).
- `test_workswarm_resume_completion.py`: adds the runtime-gated `AnswerBeforeParentParks` test, which drives `RuntimeSessionCoordinator` directly and forces the order above. It fails deterministically on the old overlay (`WAITING_FOR_CONTROL is not SUCCEEDED`) and passes with this change.

## Evidence (pinned WorkSwarm runtime, `WORKSWARM_RUNTIME_TESTS=1`, `run-focused.sh` wheel environment)

Head `1fbe45aa` (this branch, which also contains #1857's commits): every #1827 test passes, plus `test_workswarm_unload.py` (30) and `test_workswarm_completion.py`. Repeat counts are posted on #1827.

1866.author: Jianyu010
1866.body:
Closes #1859

## Cause

Beebou's stored context at `HIVE-LIVE-CHOICE-03` P3 ("时间往后推一天吧。", runs `1847-f20c4c11`, `1817-e997cc1f`, `1817-b7bf2e96`):

- The previous user turn and Beebou's reply were both about the agenda (P2).
- `list_bees` showed exactly one open task, the agenda Bee's P2 follow-up (`running`). Its routing hint said "Open tasks still belong to their listed Bee: steer the original task_ref".
- `AMBIGUITY_RULE` told Beebou to "read the conversation" and to dispatch "when a detail identifies one Bee or task", but never said what counts as a detail. The model took the last topic, or the only open task, as that detail. It steered the agenda task, sent it a `follows` update, or edited the agenda itself in 7 of 9 repeats. CHOICE-02 P4 ("Make that one a bit shorter.", after a clear offsite follow-up) has the same pattern.

So the cause is the rule's wording together with how recent work shows up in the context. No Host code chose the agenda.

## Change (prompt text only)

- `AMBIGUITY_RULE` (`selection.py`). When more than one candidate could fit, only the user's own words identify one:
  - a detail in this message that fits that task and no other;
  - their answer to a question Beebou's last reply asked;
  - a system note naming the task they chose.

  Recency is not such a detail. The topic of the previous turns, the task Beebou dispatched or reported last, and a task that is still open or running fit no better than the others, even right after a clear follow-up on one of them.
- `list_bees` `routing_hint` (`hive_beebou_tools.py`): an open task is the steer target when Beebou changes it. Being open or the latest does not make it what an unnamed message means.
- Decision: ADR-0026 amendment 2, plus contract C4 and both UPDATES logs. Rejected: a Host recency filter or roster reordering (the task stays a real candidate and needs its task_ref), and any default option.

## Tests

- `temp/hive-beebou`: the new rule phrases, the rule reaching the `list_bees` and `dispatch` descriptions, and "recency" coming before "not even the most recent". 163 passed.
- Bridge `test_hive_beebou_choice_card.py`: `routing_hint` carries the open-task sentence. The failing set of the Bridge Hive tests is identical to main's; the local venv lacks `openjiuwen`.

## Live evidence

Run `1859-96cdba16` at the head under test (full table in the PR comment):
- CHOICE-03 P3 got a card with task_refs in 2 of 3 graded repeats. It was 0 of 3 at `1847-f20c4c11` and 2 of 9 across the three earlier runs.
- P1 cards are unchanged: 3 of 3 with task_refs.
- Every clear follow-up went straight to the right Bee: CHOICE-03 P2/P4 6/6, CHOICE-02 P1/P3 4/4, CHOICE-01 P2/P4 2/2.
- FOLLOW-02/03/04 all PASS.
- Remaining recency picks: CHOICE-03 r3 P3 and CHOICE-01 r3 P1. They are recorded as rates, not gates.
