1868.author: Jianyu010
1868.body:
Refs #1784 #1749 #1790

Fixes QA #1790 R2 blocker **B11**. The Home composer sent `task.create` with one uploaded `.txt`. The device showed "消息未发送，附件已保留" (message not sent, attachment kept) and no task was created.

## Where it was dropped (Host admission, not client or relay)
- Relay log (R2 run `64e878c4`): `native_attachment_upload_accepted` (sha256 `93f1d75b…`), then `native_home_submission_forwarded action=task.create source_ids=[attachment-72c9…]` ×3. So the client request shape and the relay are fine.
- `HiveHomeTrial.send` allowed `source_ids` only with `DIGITALMATE_HIVE_INPUT_PDF_TRIAL=1`. That flag was not set on the QA Pod, so the send hit `ValueError('…plain text submissions only')` → `BAD_PARAMS` before any admission. Even with the trial on, `hold_home_pdf` refuses anything that isn't a PDF (`FORBIDDEN`).
- Behind that were two more gaps that would have hidden #1820's `inputs/` root:
  - A Bee that Beebou dispatches cites only the input's message id, so its Task input folder never got the file.
  - Beebou's copy (`read_current_home_hold`) refused non-PDF holds.

## Change
- **Admission.** With `tools.toml [inputs] enabled` and the Home trial on, the Home composer (`task.create` / `room.message`, with no quote or `follows`) admits **one** uploaded attachment of any type. It is held in the same admission transaction by `Attachments.hold_home_input`, which runs the same checks as `hold_home_pdf` minus the PDF-only rule. The PDF trial on its own keeps its PDF-only hold. With the root off, behaviour is unchanged (`BAD_PARAMS`).
- **Beebou.** `read_current_home_hold` now reads any held type (`read_pdf` still checks the PDF itself), so Beebou's `inputs/` gets the copy.
- **Bee.** On each Beebou dispatch from that input, the Host appends the input's attachment ids to `source_ids`. The append is deterministic and deduplicated, so a replay of the same operation matches. `BeeInputSources` (#1670) then places the file in the Task's input folder, as it already does for a routed send, and #1820's fence applies. Home-queue and addressed-lane dispatches cite exactly one source and are left unchanged.
- **Instruction.** Beebou's instruction names the `inputs/` path when the root is on.
- **Wiring.** `server.py` wires this at Bee-runtime composition via `dm_hive_tools.inputs.input_root_enabled()` (ownership.json updated). Contract §3 records the rule.

## Bee-page attachment entry
The entry is not hidden on purpose, and it is not a separate page. The Bee lane composer (`HiveActivityPanel.ets` `BeeSteer`) shows "添加附件" (add attachment) only when the activity index is `ready` on the live Home and the lane is an active Bee that the server reports as addressable (`target_session_ref`). In the R2 captures the device shows "连接暂不可用" (connection unavailable), from the port-forward WebSocket drops noted in §11.1. No client change in this PR. Re-check in R3 on a stable connection; if it is still absent with an active idle Bee, that is a separate client issue.

## Tests
New `tests/test_hive_home_input_attachment.py` (7). On unpatched main, 3 fail on the missing APIs and the 2 composition tests hit the same missing code. With the fix:
- the device's exact `task.create` + `.txt` frame is admitted and held, and Beebou's `inputs/` copy matches the bytes;
- the input root stays required;
- the PDF trial alone stays PDF-only;
- the dispatch append works, is deduplicated, and skips queue/addressed dispatches;
- only an admitted user input's attachments are carried;
- Bee-runtime composition wiring works with the root on and off.

Focused suites (remote 3.13 venv): this file plus `test_hive_home_input_pdf`, `test_hive_attachment_inputs`, `test_hive_home_trial`, `test_hive_home_quote_frames`, `test_hive_beebou_*`, `test_hive_bee_input_sources`, `test_hive_bee_tools`, `test_hive_owned_bee_config`, `test_hive_answer_startup`, `test_hive_bee_runtime_local_tools`, `test_hive_browser_helper_bridge`, `test_hive_session_target`, `test_hive_home_weather_trial` all pass. `temp/hive-tools/tests`: 123 passed. Architecture scan: 0 findings. The two `test_hive_document_model_reads` failures also fail on unmodified main.

Device behaviour: not to be merged until QA #1790 R3 gives P1 a PASS on this head.

1871.author: Jianyu010
1871.body:
Refs #1788 #1783 #1749 #1790

Fixes QA #1790 round-2 findings B12 (memory tools unusable) and O2 (receipts readable from Beebou's root).

## Short answers (coordinator)
- **B12a: what filtered the memory tools.** The rail only *filters* the runtime's own tool list. The Bee runtime has no memory tools. `hive-bee-effects` (`BeeEffectSocket.runtime_environment`) skipped every catalog (`agentcore`) row, so nothing listed them. Fix: catalog `bee_listing = "host"`; the Host now lists the three memory tools itself (with their handler schemas) as `mcp_hive-bee-effects_<name>`, and `runtime_names` maps them to the gate.
- **#1800 overlap.** Merged on hk with #1800 head `2aeaac3c` (merge `3f2c773e`).
  - Code and receipts paths merge cleanly. #1800's `apply_bound` receipts go through `TaskWorkspaces.receipts()`, so they land in the new directory.
  - One trivial conflict: an exposure assertion in `agent_bridge/tests/test_hive_bee_tools.py`. Resolved as the union.
  - Results on the merge: hive-tools 158 passed, hive-runtime 151 passed, Bridge Hive 285 passed with the same 9 failures as main, real runtime 2 passed, architecture check clean.
  - Whichever PR lands second merges main and takes the union. This PR will do that if #1800 lands first.

## B12a: the Bee could not see the memory tools
**Cause.** Checked in order: the rail routes a catalog name only when the Host grants it, and the Host did grant all three memory tools. But the rail only *filters* the runtime's own tool list. The Bee runtime has no `native_search_memory` / `native_read_memory` / `native_search_conversations`. The `hive-bee-effects` listing server skipped every catalog tool ("the runtime's own tools"). So nothing ever put the memory tools in front of the model. The old exposure test passed only because it fed the bare names in as if the runtime had them.

**Fix.**
- New optional catalog field `bee_listing`: `"runtime"` (default) or `"host"`. Only `agentcore` rows can use `"host"`. The three memory rows use `"host"`.
- The Host lists those rows through `hive-bee-effects` with the handler's own JSON Schema (`BeeEffectTool.input_schema`). The model sees `mcp_hive-bee-effects_native_search_memory` and the other two on its first call.
- `BeeEffectSettings.runtime_names` maps each listed name to its canonical tool. The bare name is not routed, because it is no runtime tool.
- The rail is unchanged. Each call goes to the Host gate and runs the gate reader as before.
- The listing server overrides FastMCP's public `list_tools`, so it touches no private API.

## B12b: Beebou's Global Memory search was refused
**Repro (real path, nothing seeded).** `configured_bridge` + `create_app` with live ingestion on. A WebSocket `hive.message.send` says "my QA lucky code is MEM-3A7BA7". Live ingestion publishes it to the `live.toml` Global Memory provider. Then `native_search_memory` runs through `HiveTurnService.register_hive_tools` → `_GatewayReadTool.call` (Store fence) → `PluginGateway` → `AgentCoreToolProvider`. On main this gives `No memory is available for this request.`

**Cause.** The grant, the scope (`digitalmate`/`p_local` on both sides) and the fence were all fine, and Global Memory itself returned the fact. The Gateway provider ran each handler with `asyncio.run` on a private loop in a worker thread. There, the product memory port (`HiveMemoryReads`) touched the engine's thread-bound SQLite connection and raised `ProgrammingError: SQLite objects created in a thread can only be used in that same thread`. The handler maps any product-port error to "nothing", before Global Memory is read. Ingestion lag and the #1846 fence were not involved. The existing tests called `AgentCoreTools.run` directly, so they never took this thread hop.

**Fix.**
- `AgentCoreToolProvider(host_loop=...)` runs the handler on the Host's own loop with `run_coroutine_threadsafe`, as the Bee gate reader already does. On timeout the call is cancelled there. `BeebouHostTools` records the loop from `_GatewayReadTool.call`.
- A failed product-memory read now adds nothing, but it no longer hides granted Global Memory. Fences and grants are re-checked before disclosure as before.
- `HiveGlobalMemoryReadPort.search`: the provider matches one substring (`LIKE`). When the whole query finds fewer than the limit, the port also searches each word of it, up to `global_memory.toml` `[read] max_terms = 6`. Words are split on whitespace and ASCII/CJK punctuation. Every page must come from one `surface_rev`, otherwise the search returns nothing. Example: "QA lucky code / MEM-3A7BA7" now finds the fact.

## O2: receipts out of every model-readable root
- `tools.toml` `[workspace] receipts_dir = "hive-tools-receipts"` is now relative to the DM workspace, beside `hive-tasks-host` and no longer inside it.
- The catalog refuses a `receipts_dir` that equals, contains or sits inside `tasks_dir` or `[beebou] read_root`.
- `TaskWorkspaces` refuses a receipts dir under the task directories.
- `shared_read` refuses any read root that overlaps the receipts dir. This covers Beebou's root and the skills root.
- Upgrade: at startup, `hive-tasks-host/receipts/*` moves into the new directory, link-free. A receipt already at the new place wins. If the move cannot happen, Beebou's root is refused until it can. After startup, anything at that old name is model-side data and is never imported.
- Lookup by operation ID is unchanged (`AgentCoreEffectProvider.lookup` / `bound_effect`).
- Residual risk (unchanged, contract §3): `bash` runs as the same uid and can still reach the receipts directory through the file system (B1/B2, #1840).

## Tests
- `temp/hive-tools/tests/test_hive_tools_workspace.py`:
  - receipts sit outside the task, Beebou and work roots;
  - `../../../hive-tools-receipts/…`, `../hive-tools-receipts/…`, the absolute path, a symlinked directory, a symlinked file, a relative symlink and the old `receipts/` name are all refused on the Bee and Beebou roots (read and list);
  - a read root overlapping receipts is refused;
  - legacy receipts migrate and stay found by ID, a forged post-startup legacy dir is not imported, and a legacy link is not followed.
- `test_hive_tools_read.py`: an end-to-end O2 test. A receipt written by the provider is found by `lookup`. `read_file` / `list_files` / `grep` / `glob` on both audiences, with `..`, absolute paths and symlinks, never reach it.
- `test_hive_tools_catalog.py`: receipts overlap validation.
- `test_hive_tools_memory.py`:
  - multi-word, mixed-case and CJK-punctuation queries;
  - a revision change across word pages;
  - the `max_terms` bound;
  - a failed product read does not hide Global Memory.
- `agent_bridge/tests/test_hive_beebou_memory_gateway.py`: the B12b repro above, end to end. It fails on main and passes here. It also covers `native_read_memory` of the disclosed `global:` id and a no-match query refused as nothing.
- `agent_bridge/tests/test_hive_bee_tools.py`:
  - the effect listing serves the three memory tools with the handler schemas;
  - the rail shows them on the first model call;
  - a call reaches the gate under the canonical name;
  - the bare name is not routed.
- Exposure expectations updated in `test_hive_bee_tools.py` and `test_hive_bee_product_search.py`.

## Evidence (remote test box, Python 3.13, venv from main + `install_runtime.py`, this head's `temp/` packages copied in)
- hive-tools: 134 passed. hive-runtime: 151 passed.
- Bridge Hive suites (bee_*, beebou_*, memory reads, global memory reads, live ingestion startup, attachment inputs, workswarm_bee_effects, runtime wheels, document model reads, owned bee config): 327 passed, 9 failed. All 9 fail identically on main `c58b8609` in the same environment. They are `test_hive_bee_lifecycle::test_product_bee_runtime_wires_the_pre_claim_check`, 6× `test_hive_bee_unavailable_terminal`, and 2× `test_hive_document_model_reads` (missing adapter workspace dir / harness version settings). They are not touched by this PR.
